intro.author: Paul, according to the letter (1:1). Traditionally accepted as Paul's; many modern scholars think it was written by a later follower in his name, while others defend Paul's authorship.
intro.written: If by Paul, probably about AD 62–64, between imprisonments; he planned to spend the winter at Nicopolis (3:12)
intro.audience: Titus, Paul's Gentile coworker (Galatians 2:3), whom Paul had left on the island of Crete
intro.setting: Crete is a large island in the Mediterranean with many towns. Paul had left Titus there to put the young churches in order and appoint elders in every city (1:5); Acts does not record this mission. Troublemakers, especially 'they of the circumcision' (1:10), were upsetting whole households with myths and arguments about the Law, sometimes for money.
intro.purpose: Paul instructs Titus to appoint qualified elders, silence false teachers, and teach every group in the church to live in a way that shows the goodness of the gospel.
intro.bigIdea: God's grace saves and trains believers to live good, self-controlled lives that make the gospel attractive.

outline.title: Saved by mercy for good works

commentary.t: THE EPISTLE OF PAUL TO TITUS
